mainTopic: Which verse forbids an inheritance passing between tribes through the husband, the rule that a husband does not inherit ראוי, and the משנה's 'sons of sisters'
overview: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא about the two verses in במדבר 36 that forbid a נחלה from passing from one tribe to another. It says verse 7 is about the inheritance passing through the בן, and verse 9 is about passing through the בעל. Everyone agrees verse 9 is about the בעל, so the גמרא looks for the hint in its wording. The words "איש" and "ידבקו" are rejected because they appear in both verses. רבא points to "ידבקו מטות", and רב אשי points to "אחר", since a son is not 'another' to his mother. Next, a chain of אמוראים teaches that a husband inherits what his wife already held (מוחזק) but not what was only due to her (ראוי). The proofs are יאיר and פנחס, sons who owned land their fathers never had, and the גמרא explains why the second proof is needed. Finally the גמרא turns to the משנה's phrase 'sons of sisters', and a ברייתא says it means sons and not daughters.

steps.title: Another teaching: the verse is about the husband
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא teaches that "ולא תסב נחלה ממטה למטה אחר" (במדבר 36:9) speaks about an inheritance passing to another tribe through the בעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: "So shall no inheritance transfer from one tribe to another tribe." This verse is talking about an inheritance passing over through the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא that explains what the verse "ממטה למטה אחר" is warning about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who inherits land and marries a man from another tribe could cause her land to leave her tribe, because her בעל inherits from her. This ברייתא says verse 9 is aimed at exactly that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall transfer, turn over (from one owner to another)
Transfer through the husband, who inherits from his wife

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"So shall no inheritance transfer
from one tribe to another tribe"
the verse speaks of transfer by means of the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא on the same verses discussed just before this amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Verse 9 ("ממטה למטה אחר") forbids the inheritance passing to another tribe through the בעל.

steps.title: Maybe the verse is about the son?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks itself whether verse 9 might instead be about the inheritance passing through the בן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is about transfer through the husband? Or maybe it is only about transfer through the son?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. It suggests that verse 9 might really be about the son, and this sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son can also carry land out of his mother's tribe, because he inherits from his mother but belongs to his father's tribe. So the ברייתא must show why verse 9 is about the בעל and not the בן.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say (a standard way a ברייתא opens a challenge to itself)
Transfer through the son, who inherits from his mother

phrases.english: Do you say it is about transfer by means of the husband;
or is it only about transfer by means of the son?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading given in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is verse 9 about the בעל or about the בן?

steps.title: The son is already covered by the other verse
steps.stepSummary: Verse 7 ("ממטה אל מטה") already speaks about the בן, so verse 9 must be teaching about the בעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תורה says, "So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel transfer from tribe to tribe," transfer through the son is already stated. So how do I explain "So shall no inheritance transfer from one tribe to another tribe"? It speaks of transfer through the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The son's case is already in an earlier verse, so the later verse must be about the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that the תורה does not repeat itself for nothing. Since verse 7 already covers the בן, verse 9 must add something new: the בעל.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain (what is this verse for?)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, verse 7 ("ממטה אל מטה") is about the בן, and verse 9 ("ממטה למטה אחר") is about the בעל.

phrases.english: When it says:
"So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel transfer
from tribe to tribe"
here transfer by means of the son is stated;
so how do I explain
"So shall no inheritance transfer from one tribe to another tribe"?
The verse speaks of transfer by means of the husband.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Verse 7 already covers the בן, so verse 9 must be about the בעל.

steps.title: Everyone agrees, but where is the hint?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that both ברייתות agree that "ממטה למטה אחר" is about the בעל, and asks how the wording shows this.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that "from one tribe to another tribe" speaks of transfer through the husband. How is this shown in the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what both ברייתות share. Then it asks which word in the verse shows that it is about the husband. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות may argue about other details, but on this point they agree. The גמרא now wants an actual hint in the words of the פסוק, not only the logic of avoiding repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: At any rate, in any case
What shows this? Where is it implied?

phrases.english: In any event, according to everyone,
phrases.notes: "Everyone" means both ברייתות, the earlier one and this one.

phrases.english: "from one tribe to another tribe"
the verse speaks of transfer by means of the husband;
from where is this inferred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a shared point from the ברייתות and asks for its source in the wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which word in verse 9 shows that it is about the בעל?

steps.title: The word "man" means husband
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא says the hint is the word "איש" in the verse, which can mean husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory sign. רבה בר רב שילא said: The verse says "איש" (man).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא answers that the word "איש" in the verse is what shows it is about a husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Verse 9 ends: "for each one (איש) of the tribes shall cleave to its own inheritance." Since "איש" is often used for a husband, he reads it as a hint to the בעל.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign to help remember the speakers or answers

phrases.english: A mnemonic.
Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
The verse states: "Each one [ish]."
phrases.notes: The word אִישׁ also means husband, as in "אלימלך איש נעמי" (רות 1:3).

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא אָמַר קְרָא אִישׁ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "איש" hints at a husband.

steps.title: Both verses say "man"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר רב שילא: the word "איש" appears in both verses, so it cannot show that only verse 9 is about the בעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But "איש" is written in both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from "איש", because the son's verse uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Verse 7 also says "כי איש בנחלת מטה אבתיו ידבקו". If "איש" meant husband, verse 7 would also be about the בעל. So the word cannot separate the two verses.

phrases.english: But "ish" is written in both of them!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב שילא's proof from "איש"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word found in both verses cannot show that only one of them is about the בעל.

steps.title: The word "shall cleave" hints at marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a different hint: the word "ידבקו", which recalls a man cleaving to his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The verse says "ידבקו" (shall cleave).
steps.whatsHappening: Since "איש" failed, רב נחמן בר יצחק suggests a different word from the verse as the hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ידבקו" recalls "ודבק באשתו" (בראשית 2:24), language of marriage. So he reads it as a hint to the בעל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and offers a new one)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
The verse states: "Shall cleave."
phrases.notes: This recalls "ודבק באשתו" (בראשית 2:24), a man cleaving to his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 5 with a new hint.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the proof with a different word from the verse
steps.terutzMaskana: The hint is the word "ידבקו", language of marriage.

steps.title: Both verses say "shall cleave"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק in the same way: "ידבקו" also appears in both verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: But "ידבקו" is written in both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same problem against the second answer. The son's verse also uses "ידבקו".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Verse 7 ends with "ידבקו" just like verse 9. So this word also cannot show that only verse 9 is about the בעל, and the search for the hint continues.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question is finished here. The same challenge has hit both answers, and the next two steps (רבא and רב אשי) give hints that only verse 9 has.

phrases.english: But "shall cleave" is written in both of them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof in step 7 the same way step 6 attacked step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof from "ידבקו"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word found in both verses cannot show that only one of them is about the בעל.

steps.title: רבא: 'The tribes shall cleave' points to marriage
steps.stepSummary: After both earlier hints failed, רבא brings a new hint: the phrase 'ידבקו מטות', 'the tribes shall cleave'. Tribes become attached to each other through marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The פסוק says, 'The tribes shall cleave.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to the question of how we know the second פסוק is about the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'איש' and 'ידבקו' were rejected because each one appears in both פסוקים. רבא points instead to the full phrase 'ידבקו מטות'. Only verse 9 has it, because verse 7 says 'ידבקו בני ישראל'. Tribes 'cleave' to each other through marriage, so this פסוק fits a husband inheriting his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It sets aside the earlier answers.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The verse states: "The tribes shall cleave."

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רבא אמר קרא ידבקו מטות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the hint of רב נחמן בר יצחק, which step 8 knocked down.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The single words 'איש' or 'ידבקו' were thought to show the פסוק is about the husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase 'tribes cleaving' describes joining through marriage, so the פסוק is about the בעל.

steps.title: רב אשי: A son is not 'another'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different hint: the word 'אחר' ('another tribe'). A son is not 'another' person compared with his mother, so this פסוק must be talking about the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The פסוק says 'from one tribe to another tribe', and a son is not 'another'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second new answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a son inherits his mother, the land does not really move to 'another', because he counts as an extension of her. Verse 9 says 'למטה אחר' ('to another tribe'), while verse 7 only says 'ממטה אל מטה'. So the verse with 'אחר' must mean the husband, who really is a separate person.
steps.whatToRemember: The search for a hint ends with two good answers: רבא's 'ידבקו מטות' (marriage joins tribes) and רב אשי's 'אחר' (a son is not 'another', so it means the husband).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: The verse states:
"From one tribe to another tribe"
and a son is not "another."
phrases.notes: He means a son is like a continuation of his mother, so the only true 'other' would be the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב אשי אמר אמר קרא ממטה למטה אחר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel answer next to רבא's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might be about a son inheriting his mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a son is not 'another', the word 'אחר' shows the פסוק is about the husband.

steps.title: A husband does not inherit property that was only 'due' to his wife
steps.stepSummary: A long chain of names, ending with רבי or רבי יהושע בן קרחה, teaches that a בעל does not inherit ראוי the way he inherits מוחזק. The source is the פסוק about שגוב and יאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי ינאי, in the name of רבי, and some say it was in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: How do we know that a husband does not take property that was only due to his wife the way he takes what she already held? Because the פסוק says, 'And שגוב fathered יאיר, who had twenty-three cities in the land of גלעד.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא states a rule about what a husband inherits and points to a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוחזק is property the wife already owned while she was alive, and her husband inherits it. ראוי is property that would have come to her later, for example from a relative who died after she did. The husband does not get the ראוי. The פסוק will be explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And some traced it to the name of
Property 'due' to someone that they do not hold yet
Property someone already owns and holds

steps.confusionAlert: The rule does not say the husband inherits nothing from his wife. He does inherit what she already held (מוחזק). He only loses out on what was still 'on the way' to her (ראוי).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule in the laws of a husband inheriting his wife, and it comes up often in the rest of the פרק.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says
that Rabbi Yannai says that Rabbi says,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָטוּ בָּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה:
phrases.english: and some traced it to the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa:
From where is it derived that a husband does not take
property that is due as he takes property that is held?
phrases.notes: 'Due' means property she would have gotten had she lived, like an inheritance from a relative who died after her. 'Held' means what she already owned.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And Seguv begot Yair,"
"who had twenty-three cities"
"in the land of Gilead."

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אבהו אמר רבי יוחנן אמר רבי ינאי אמר רבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about what a husband inherits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband inherits his wife's מוחזק but not her ראוי.

steps.title: How יאיר got cities his father never had
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof. יאיר had cities that שגוב never had, so they must have come through his mother. She died before the relatives she would have inherited, so her son inherited that property and her husband did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did יאיר get land that שגוב did not have? This teaches that שגוב married a woman, and she died while the people she would have inherited from were still alive. Then those people died, and יאיר inherited what was due to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the פסוק about יאיר proves the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a son gets land from his father. If יאיר had cities that שגוב never owned, they came from somewhere else. The answer is his mother's ראוי. If a husband inherited ראוי, שגוב would have owned the cities, so the פסוק shows he did not.

keyTerms.meaning: The people she would have inherited from

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְיָאִיר – שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לִשְׂגוּב?
phrases.english: From where did Yair have land that Seguv did not have?
Rather, this teaches that Seguv married a woman,
and she died in the lifetime of her legators;
and her legators died, and Yair inherited it from her.
phrases.notes: יאיר is her son. Her husband שגוב got none of this property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מנין ליאיר שלא היה לו לשגוב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 11 proves the rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a husband does not inherit ראוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א ב:כב: יאיר had cities שגוב never had.

steps.title: A second proof: פנחס had a hill his father never had
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק says that אלעזר was buried on the hill of פנחס his son. פנחס owned land that אלעזר never had, so he must have inherited it through his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק also says: 'And אלעזר son of אהרן died, and they buried him...' Where did פנחס get land that אלעזר did not have? This teaches that אלעזר married a woman, and she died while the people she would have inherited from were still alive. Then they died, and פנחס inherited what was due to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second proof for the same rule, built the same way as the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as with יאיר. A son owns land his father never owned, so it came from his mother's ראוי. This shows again that the husband did not inherit it.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says. It brings an extra פסוק.
Etc.; the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: And it says: "And Elazar, the son of Aaron, died,"
"and they buried him, etc."
phrases.notes: יהושע כד:לג. The rest says they buried him on the hill of פנחס his son.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְפִנְחָס – שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לְאֶלְעָזָר?
phrases.english: From where did Pinehas have land that Elazar did not have?
This teaches that Elazar married a woman,
and she died in the lifetime of her legators;
and her legators died, and Pinehas inherited it from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel proof added after the first.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a husband does not inherit ראוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע כד:לג: פנחס had a hill אלעזר never had.

steps.title: Why is a second proof needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the extra פסוק ('ואומר') was brought when the first proof seemed enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does it say 'and it also says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a second proof is needed. This sets up the explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second proof means the first one could be read some other way. The גמרא wants to find out what weakness in the יאיר proof the פנחס proof fixes.

phrases.english: And what is the reason for "and it says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why step 13 was added to step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What gap in the יאיר proof makes the פנחס proof necessary?

steps.title: The יאיר proof could mean יאיר inherited his own wife
steps.stepSummary: The proof from יאיר is weak. Maybe יאיר himself married a woman and inherited from his own wife, so the cities never came from his mother. The פסוק about אלעזר fixes this, because it ties the land to אלעזר and his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that יאיר married a woman who died, and he inherited her, the פסוק teaches: 'And אלעזר son of אהרן died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first proof can be pushed aside, so the second proof is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cities of יאיר might have come from his own wife and not from his mother. That would prove nothing about a husband and ראוי. The אלעזר פסוק is linked to the father and his death, which points to an inheritance that skipped אלעזר and went to his son.

phrases.english: And if you would say: Yair,
who married a woman and she died, and he inherited her;

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְאֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן מֵת״.
phrases.english: the verse states: "And Elazar, the son of Aaron, died."

steps.triggerLanguage: וכי תימא יאיר דהוה נסיב איתתא ומתה וירתה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יאיר proof could be explained as יאיר inheriting his own wife, so the אלעזר פסוק is needed.

steps.title: The word 'his son' blocks the idea that פנחס got a priest's field
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say פנחס, as a כהן, got the land as a שדה חרמים (a field dedicated to כהנים). The פסוק says 'his son', which shows it was an inheritance due to אלעזר that his son inherited.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say the land came to פנחס as a dedicated field, the פסוק says 'his son'. That means an inheritance that was due to אלעזר, and his son inherited it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks one last way of escaping the פנחס proof and so finishes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פנחס got the hill as a שדה חרמים given to a כהן, the proof would fail. The word 'בנו' frames the land as something that passed from father to son as inheritance. So it was ראוי that would have gone to אלעזר through his wife, and it went to the son instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A field dedicated to the Temple and given to כהנים
An inheritance that was due to him

steps.whatToRemember: A husband inherits what his wife already held (מוחזק) but not what was only due to her (ראוי). The proofs are יאיר's cities and פנחס's hill: land the sons had and their fathers never had.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא דִּנְפַלָה לֵיהּ בִּשְׂדֵה חֲרָמִים,
phrases.english: And if you would say that it came to him as a dedicated field,
phrases.notes: פנחס was a כהן, and כהנים could receive fields that were dedicated to the Temple.

phrases.english: the verse states: "his son",
an inheritance that was due to him, and his son inherited it.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is אלעזר. The land should have reached him through his wife, but his son got it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וכי תימא דנפלה ליה בשדה חרמים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a remaining gap in the פנחס proof from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פנחס might have received the land as a שדה חרמים because he was a כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בנו' shows it was an inheritance due to the father that went to the son, so the husband does not inherit ראוי.

steps.title: The ברייתא limits the משנה's phrase to sons of sisters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'and sons of sisters' and brings a ברייתא that says this means sons of sisters, not daughters of sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And sons of sisters.' A ברייתא teaches: sons of sisters, and not daughters of sisters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next phrase of the משנה, 'sons of sisters.' It then brings a ברייתא that defines the phrase more exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists sons of sisters among relatives who inherit from a person but do not pass an inheritance to him. The ברייתא adds that the משנה means sons of sisters specifically, and not daughters of sisters. So the ברייתא narrows the משנה's wording to the males it names.

keyTerms.meaning: Sons of sisters: nephews born to the dead man's sisters
Daughters of sisters: nieces born to the dead man's sisters

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא reads the משנה's 'sons of sisters' exactly: it means sons, not daughters.

phrases.english: And sons of sisters.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's list of relatives who inherit from someone but do not pass an inheritance on to him.

phrases.english: It was taught: sons of sisters,
and not daughters of sisters.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: בְּנֵי אָחוֹת, וְלֹא בְּנוֹת אָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of a son inheriting through his mother (יאיר, פנחס) and moves to the next phrase in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's phrase 'sons of sisters' covers sons of sisters and not daughters of sisters.
